page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is bundled, providing a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 24294.54 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8497.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 934.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 946.78 GB/sec, though uncached large-block writes drop to 67.98 GB/sec. The instance delivers average results in software compilation with a score of 14961.0 and ray tracing with a score of 13891.0.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation, the c6gd.4xlarge offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage makes it well-suited for applications requiring low-latency scratch space. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and distributed data processing where high-speed local storage and compute-heavy ARM execution are beneficial.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.4xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based instance powered by 16 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers balanced multi-core performance, as shown by its stress-ng multi-core score of 24294.54 and average software compilation benchmarks. While single-core performance and cryptographic execution are relatively weak, its high-speed local storage and solid multi-threaded capabilities make it qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads. The c6gd.4xlarge is best suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation tasks that benefit from dedicated ARM cores and low-latency local storage.
